messages:
cheng: Quick heads up — I'm sketching a proposal to merge 'duplicate' trace keys at ingest to reduce cardinality. cc @rita @sam

rita: interesting. are you thinking we canonicalize keys or collapse them? worried about losing attribution for billing

sam: merging helps storage and index size but can break tenant-level attribution if keys are shared. i'd prefer a deterministic canonicalize(key) + keep original in metadata for edge cases :thinking_face:

maria: for high-cardinality services this could drop cardinality a lot. but watch memory/CPU on ingest. any plan for fallback when memory spikes? :warning:

cheng: rough hybrid idea:

```
# pseudocode
def normalize_key(key):
  # split on common prefixes, hash tail
  prefix, tail = split_prefix(key)
  return f"{prefix}:{sha1(tail)[:8]}"
```

store normalized in `trace.key`, keep `trace.orig_keys` as array only when orig != normalized (configurable). default: don't store orig to save bytes.

infra-bot: RFC draft created: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/telemetry/mergeable-trace-keys-2026 (ops:cheng)

sam: two questions — schema: should orig go under `observability.trace.orig_keys` or `trace.orig_keys`? and do we need a migration plan for older dashboards?

rita: prefer `observability.*` namespace for anything we might later export. dashboards: we can add translation layer in console for 6 months

maria: also consider how this interacts with sampling. if we merge before sampling we get better compress, but risk biasing sampling if collapse skews token distribution

cheng: good point. proposal: merge after sampling for correctness, but allow an option to merge pre-sample for bulky tenants who opt-in. actionable: i'll write RFC with tradeoffs + perf numbers. intended owners: eng-platform + ingestion. timeline: prototype next sprint, perf tests after.

rita: :+1: please include an example diff of event size reduction and estimated savings

sam: i'll volunteer to review and run local ingest sim

cheng: thanks — will ping when draft's up.
